newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Timah to buy mining firms.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Timah to buy mining firms.

text.p: Indonesian tin miner PT Tambang Timah plans to acquire five domestic and foreign mining companies as part of its diversification programme, Timah's President Director Erry Hardjapamekas said on Thursday.

"We plan to acquire the foreign and domestic mining companies as soon as possible. I can't say when exactly, but I hope it is going to be this year," Hardjapamekas told the company's annual general meeting.
He said Timah was currently diversifying into diamonds, coal and gold.
"It's too risky to only focus on a single commodity," he said, declining to give the names of the companies or the amount of money to be used to acquire them.
The acquisitions could be funded through loans and surplus funds, he added.

Hardjapamekas said Timah had accepted the decision by the Minister of Mines and Energy Ida Bagus Sudjana that the company would not participate in the exploration stage of the lucrative Busang gold find in East Kalimantan.
"We accept the government's decision. As the chairman of the company I am dissappointed but that's not the end," he said.
The government has not ruled out the participation of state-owned companies in the exploitation stage of the Busang mine.

Hardjapamekas said the 150 billion rupiah initially intended to be used by Timah to bid for a share in the Busang project would be used for other projects, including the exploration for gold in North Sumatra, Central Kalimantan and East Java.

He also told the meeting Timah, formerly a state-owned company listed in Jakarta and London in 1995, would declare total dividends worth 46.7 billion rupiah for 1996, an equivalent of 92.76 rupiah per share or 41.38 percent higher than in 1995.
